subject: history_social
passage: The Kallanai, a dam across the Kaveri River in Tamil Nadu, India, is often described as one of the oldest water-control structures still in use. Tradition credits it to the Chola king Karikalan, who ruled nearly two thousand years ago. <u>Built of unshaped stones piled across the riverbed, the dam slowed the river and sent part of its flow into channels that watered nearby fields.</u> Repaired many times since, it still serves farmers today.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It argues that the dam should be replaced with a modern structure.
choices.B: It explains how the dam was built and how it helped farmers.
choices.C: It identifies the ruler who is traditionally credited with the dam.
choices.D: It suggests that the dam no longer serves any practical purpose.

explanation.why: The underlined sentence describes the dam's construction ("unshaped stones piled across the riverbed") and what it did: it sent water "into channels that watered nearby fields." It explains how the dam was made and how it supported farming.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never suggests replacing the dam; it notes that the dam still serves farmers.
explanation.B: Correct. The sentence tells what the dam was made of and how it moved river water to the fields.
explanation.C: Incorrect. King Karikalan is named in the previous sentence, not in the underlined one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The last sentence says the dam "still serves farmers today," and the underlined sentence describes its usefulness.
